ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a horizontal wire below connecting the left and right branches, which can be selected as the common reference node. The left branch is a voltage source labeled 12V, with its lower end marked with a positive sign and its upper end marked with a negative sign; the upper-left node is connected to the upper output node on the right through the diode D at the top. The right branch, from top to bottom, is a 3kΩ resistor and a voltage source labeled 9V; the lower end of the 9V source is connected to the lower common wire and is marked with a positive sign, and the upper end is marked with a negative sign. U0 is labeled between the upper and lower terminals on the right. Reasoning: Take the lower common wire as 0V. Since the lower end of the 12V source is positive and the upper end is negative, the potential of the upper-left node is -12V; since the lower end of the 9V source is positive and the upper end is negative, the potential of the upper end of the 9V source is -9V. The diode D connects from the upper-left node to the upper output node on the right. Comparing the potentials at its two ends: the left side is -12V, and the right side corresponds to -9V when there is no current through the 3kΩ resistor. The left side is not higher than the right side, so the diode is reverse-biased, does not conduct, and can be regarded as an open circuit. After the diode is open-circuited, there is no current in the 3kΩ resistor and no voltage drop across the resistor, so the potential of the upper output node equals the potential of the upper end of the 9V source, namely -9V. According to the output voltage reference in the problem figure, U0 = -9V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the lower horizontal conductor as the common reference node, the 9 V source in the right branch under the 3 kΩ resistor, the 12 V source in the left branch, and diode D connecting the left-top node to the upper output node. Choose the lower rail as 0 V. From the polarity marks of the sources, write the voltage of the node at the top of the 9 V source and the voltage of the node at the top of the 12 V source. Compare these two node voltages in the direction of diode D to decide whether D is forward or reverse biased. The comparison shows D is not conducting, so the diode is an open circuit. Then no current flows through the 3 kΩ resistor, so the upper output node has the same potential as the top of the 9 V source. Report the algebraic voltage U0 according to the output reference in the problem, giving U0 = -9 V.

After the diode is open-circuited, there is no current in the 3kΩ resistor and no voltage drop across the resistor, so the potential of the upper output node equals the potential of the upper end of the 9V source, namely -9V. According to the output voltage reference in the problem figure, U0 = -9V.
